headline_marked: Apple to enable [[iPhone-Windows PC copy-paste]] by Fall 2027
headline: Apple to enable iPhone-Windows PC copy-paste by Fall 2027
summary: Microsoft requested the feature under EU interoperability rules. Apple has agreed to develop a solution using its AccessorySetupKit.
details: Apple has confirmed it will develop a feature allowing seamless copy-pasting between iPhones and Windows PCs. This initiative stems from a request made by Microsoft through Apple's EU interoperability request system, established to comply with the Digital Markets Act.

Microsoft asked for a persistent clipboard access mechanism that wouldn't require apps to be foregrounded or users to repeatedly grant permission. The goal is to replicate the ease of Apple's Universal Clipboard, which works across its own devices.

In response, Apple stated it will introduce a new solution utilizing its AccessorySetupKit, the same framework used for smartwatches to receive iPhone notifications. Users will need to consent to clipboard sharing with paired accessories once.

The company acknowledges this as a "significant engineering effort" and aims to complete development by Fall 2027. The feature will initially be beta-tested for a wide release in the European Union, with availability elsewhere yet to be confirmed.
caption:
Apple is bringing its Universal Clipboard functionality to Windows PCs.

headline_marked: [[EU AI Act]] applies to chatbots as of August 2nd, 2026
headline: EU AI Act applies to chatbots as of August 2nd, 2026
summary: New transparency duties are now live for AI systems generating content for EU users. Developers can use open-source tools to help comply.
details: The EU AI Act's Article 50, concerning transparency duties for AI-generated content, officially began applying on August 2nd, 2026. This means any chatbot or AI system that generates text, images, audio, or video for users within the European Union must now adhere to these regulations.

To address the complexity of the Act, an open-source tool called Legalithm has been developed. It functions as an MCP server, compatible with environments like Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex, allowing developers to query compliance requirements.

Legalithm offers four key tools: classify, explain_obligation, generate_disclosure, and check_record. The first three operate entirely offline, with the rule corpus bundled locally, ensuring no data leaves the user's machine. This provides a secure and private way to assess AI compliance.

The tool provides detailed feedback, including matched rules, the recency of the corpus, and confidence scores, differentiating it from standard LLM queries. A crucial design choice is its 'reviewRequired' flag, which defers to human review when confidence is low, preventing confidently incorrect assertions.

Legalithm is free and open-source, aiming to remain accessible through the high-risk compliance deadlines. The developers are actively seeking feedback on classification accuracy to further improve the tool's effectiveness.
